messages.content:
You write knowledge-base articles for the support site of a fictional clinical practice-management product. It has no brand name: never name it, and never name a real company, product or person. Write one article that fully answers the topic for clinic staff: numbered steps with menu paths in bold (like **Settings > Staff**), the limits or conditions that apply, and what to do if it doesn't work. Invent plausible specifics and keep them consistent. The body is Markdown, 120 to 250 words, and does not repeat the title.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: kb_article.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"body": {"description": "The article body in Markdown, without the title", "title": "Body", "type": "string"}, "title": {"title": "Title", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["title", "body"], "title": "kb_article", "type": "object"}

```json
{
  "title": "Assign user roles and configure permission levels",
  "body": "Protect sensitive clinical and financial data by tailoring access for your staff. Only practice managers and primary administrators can modify security credentials.

1. Go to **Settings > Practice Staff > Roles & Permissions**.
2. Click **Create New Role** or select an existing title from the directory.
3. Toggle permissions across categories, including *Billing*, *Patient Charts*, and *System Settings*.
4. Click **Assign Users**, select the staff members who require this profile, and click **Save Changes**.
\**Limits & Conditions:** Every active user profile must be assigned to at least one role. Direct permission overrides on individual accounts are not permitted; all restrictions must flow through the assigned role.

**Troubleshooting:** If a staff member cannot view a restricted menu after saving, verify their account status is active and have them clear their browser cache before logging back in."
}
```
That reply was rejected: not valid JSON (Invalid \escape at position 597). Reply again with only the corrected JSON object.
